newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Death, jail sentences upheld in Vietnam drugs case. [CORRECTED 13:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Death, jail sentences upheld in Vietnam drugs case. [CORRECTED 13:25 GMT]

text.p: A Vietnam court has rejected appeals by eight people who were sentenced to death for their part in a heroin-trafficking ring, a court official said on Tuesday.
The court also upheld life imprisonment sentences for six (corrects from seven) other members of the syndicate and various jail terms for five (corrects from four) others.
The exposure of the syndicate and the trial of its key figures in May embarrassed the Interior Ministry because several police officers and border guards were involved.
State prosecutors last week recommended that appeals for leniency by the 19 of the 22 convicted in May's high-profile trial should be turned down.
Even former police captain Vu Xuan Truong, the crime ring's kingpin and now a household name in Vietnam, had finally admitted to the Supreme Appeals Court that he deserved to die.

"I...was an especially dangerous criminal for Vietnamese people and people in the world," newspapers reported him as saying. "My crimes, condemned by Vietnamese people and people in the world, deserve the death sentence one thousand times over."

A further 40 people are due to stand trial soon for their part in the ring, which flooded Vietnam with hundreds of kilograms of heroin from the notorious "Golden Triangle" area where Laos, Burma and Thailand meet.
